analysis.session_summary: Across Asia, London, and NY morning, GBP led with +0.269% strength while USD was weakest at -0.232%. A downside UK average earnings surprise strengthened GBP, an inverted reaction that set the tone for GBP/USD +66.9 pips. Most other currency moves lacked clear catalysts, with broad USD and CHF underperformance keeping USD/CHF nearly flat at -0.7 pips. Late Iran-US headlines triggered sharp reversals in CHF/JPY and oil.

themes.theme: GBP exceptionalism on inverted UK data
themes.evidence: Average Earnings Index 3m/y missed at 3.7% vs 3.8% forecast but GBP strengthened 0.106%; GBP was top strength at +0.269% and GBP/USD closed +66.9 pips.

themes.theme: Broad USD and CHF underperformance without clear catalysts
themes.evidence: USD strength was -0.232% and CHF -0.222%, the two weakest; USD/CHF closed -0.7 pips despite both moving, with no own releases for either.

themes.theme: Late Iran headline caused sharp reversals
themes.evidence: CHF/JPY rose 12.6 pips in its final leg after 'Iran-US talks continue, reports that the deal is close are wrong' hit around 17:00.

currency_drivers.USD: No clear catalyst: USD fell broadly, with no US data or event explaining the move.
currency_drivers.EUR: No clear catalyst: EUR was soft, with only weak German headlines too weak to own the move.
currency_drivers.JPY: No clear catalyst: JPY was broadly flat, with a failed early bid and no own data.
currency_drivers.GBP: UK Average Earnings Index miss produced an inverted GBP rally, lifting GBP across the board.
currency_drivers.AUD: No clear catalyst: AUD selling was rejected, recovering 84% without an own data trigger.
currency_drivers.CAD: No clear catalyst: CAD selling rejected, recovering 71% with no Canada-specific catalyst.
currency_drivers.CHF: No clear catalyst: CHF gave back an early gain fully, ending as one of the weakest.
currency_drivers.NZD: No clear catalyst: NZD held its range and was second-strongest on broad USD weakness.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD carved four uncaused legs (+26.0, -30.0, +53.0, -26.3 pips) for a net +19.3 pip close, with USD weakness providing the bid against soft EUR.

polarity_reads.read: A downside wage surprise strengthened GBP by 0.106%, an inverted reaction that implies the market was not positioned for a dovish repricing; it hints at stale short GBP or expectations that the BoE will look through soft wages.

scenarios.name: GBP continuation after UK CPI
scenarios.thesis: UK CPI y/y (forecast 3.4%, previous 3.1%) prints hot or Bailey sounds hawkish, extending the inverted GBP bid.
triggers: UK CPI y/y at or above 3.4%
BOE Gov Bailey emphasizes upside inflation risks
scenarios.invalidation: CPI surprise below 3.1% or Bailey emphasizes downside growth risks

scenarios.thesis: USD weakness is overdone; with no US data, the dollar catches a bid against commodity FX while GBP holds its gain.
